title: House Fly (Musca domestica) Laboratory Rearing Protocol
author: Levi Zahn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vbse2ne

steps.title: Prepare oviposition cup
steps.instruction: Place a Kimwipe into a 1.5 oz condiment cup, add ~5 mL evaporated milk, put the cup into a cage containing >5‑day‑old adult flies, and leave for 24 h for egg deposition.

steps.title: Soak alfalfa pellets
steps.instruction: Combine 3 parts alfalfa pellets (1 cup, 240 mL) with 1 part deionized water (~80 mL), mix, and refrigerate for at least 24 h; pellets can be stored up to 3 months.

steps.title: Prepare larval media
steps.instruction: In a large plastic container combine 3 Tbsp (15 mL) baker’s fast‑rising yeast, 1 cup (240 mL) non‑fat dry milk, and the soaked alfalfa slurry; add 1 L deionized water and mix thoroughly. Then add 16 cups (3.75 L) red flaky wheat bran and the remaining 2 L deionized water; stir until the mixture is moist enough to clump. Evenly divide the media between two 5 cm‑high larval rearing pans (≈3.8 cm depth).

steps.title: Transfer eggs to pans
steps.instruction: Retrieve the oviposition cup, place a #25 sieve over a #200 sieve, and rinse the cup with cool tap water to release the Kimwipe and eggs. Unfold the Kimwipe and rinse the eggs through the sieves into the #200 sieve. Tilt the #200 sieve and collect the egg suspension with a 15 mL centrifuge tube, letting it settle 30 s; keep only the bottom 1 mL of viable (sinking) eggs. Invert the tube 3–4 times to suspend the eggs, then pour the 1 mL egg slurry into one larval pan; repeat for the second pan. Cover each pan with a fine mesh sock, secure with a knot or two rubber bands, and incubate at 26 °C (45 % RH).

substeps.instruction: Rinse oviposition cup to free Kimwipe and eggs.
Unfold Kimwipe and rinse eggs through sieves.
Collect egg suspension in 15 mL tube; let settle 30 s.
Retain 1 mL of sinking eggs; invert tube 3–4 times.
Pour eggs into larval pan; repeat for second pan.
Cover pans with mesh sock and secure with rubber bands.

steps.title: Place pans in dry bran
steps.instruction: After 5 days at 26 °C, when larvae are in the final (L3) stage and the media is dark brown and loose, place each larval pan into a larger plastic container (18 QT) containing 2–4 L dry bran, ensuring the pan does not touch the container walls.

steps.title: Flood pans to release larvae
steps.instruction: Add deionized water to each larval pan until the water reaches approximately half the height of the larval media (≈1.5 L, depending on density). Within 15–30 min larvae will emerge, climb out of the pan, and burrow into the surrounding dry bran to pupate. Cover both containers with fine mesh socks secured with two rubber bands and allow 3 days for pupation.

steps.title: Sift pupae from bran
steps.instruction: Remove the larval pans, scrape any pupae stuck to the pan bottom, freeze the wet media or discard it, then use a #10 sieve to sift the dry bran; pupae are retained while bran passes through. Collect all pupae and mix from both pans to maintain genetic similarity (≈5 000 pupae per 1 mL eggs).

steps.title: Set up adult fly cage
steps.instruction: Place a wire cage with a mesh sleeve inside an 11.4 QT dishpan. Add 250 mL of mixed pupae (≈2 000 adults) into a lid‑less container within the cage to allow emergence. Provide a water cup containing two paper towels soaked to the halfway mark, and a food dish of powdered milk and table sugar mixed 1:1. Secure the mesh sleeve end with a rubber band. Store any excess pupae in mesh‑top containers at 15 °C (60 °F) for up to a week as a backup.

substeps.instruction: Insert wire cage with mesh sleeve into dishpan.
Add 250 mL mixed pupae to a lid‑less container inside the cage.
Place water cup with two paper towels; fill water to halfway up towels.
Add food dish (powdered milk : table sugar = 1:1).
Secure mesh sleeve with rubber band.
Store surplus pupae at 15 °C in mesh‑top containers for up to one week.

steps.title: Maintain adult cages
steps.instruction: Check adult cages every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday; replenish water and food as needed. No weekend checks are required.
